title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    4| class TokenCore:
    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21| 
   22| A local copy is also available in the `data/` folder.
   23| 
   24| ## Installation
   25| 
   26| ```bash
   27| git clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git
   28| cd TokenCore
   29| pip install -r requirements.txt
   30| ```
   31| 
   32| ## Quick Start
   33| 
   34| ```python
   35| from TokenCore import TextCore
   36| 
   37| model = TokenCore()
   38| 
   39| # Fit on normal token embeddings
   40| model.fit(X_train)
   41| 
   42| # Get token-level anomaly scores

   44| ```
   45| 
   46| `X_train` and `X_test` are token embedding matrices (e.g. BERT embeddings with max-pooling over subwords). See `Demo.ipynb` for the full pipeline, including embedding extraction, token-level scoring, and document-level aggregation.

import json
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

d = np.load(DATA / "grammar.npy", allow_pickle=True).item()
print("keys:", list(d.keys()))
sentences, tokens, labels = d["sentences"], d["tokens"], d["labels"]
print("n docs:", len(sentences), len(tokens), len(labels))

"""Load the released Grammar benchmark and build the 50%-normal train/test split.

The released artifact is repo/data/grammar.npy, a pickled dict with keys
'sentences' (list of [sentence]), 'tokens' (list of gold word tokens) and
'labels' (list of 0/1 token labels), produced by the authors'
tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py from the Label Studio export
grammar_correction_labeled.json.  This is exactly the object Demo.ipynb loads.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
DATA_DIR = REPO / "repo" / "data"


@dataclass
class Document:
    doc_id: int
    sentence: str
    words: list
    token_labels: list
    doc_label: int = 0

    @property
    def n_tokens(self) -> int:
        return len(self.words)


@dataclass
class Split:
    train: list = field(default_factory=list)   # list[Document], normal only
    test: list = field(default_factory=list)    # list[Document], normal + anomalous
    seed: int = 0
    train_fraction: float = 0.5


def load_grammar(data_dir: Path | None = None) -> list:
    """Return the 300 Grammar documents with gold word-level token labels."""
    data_dir = Path(data_dir) if data_dir else DATA_DIR
    raw = np.load(data_dir / "grammar.npy", allow_pickle=True).item()
    sentences, tokens, labels = raw["sentences"], raw["tokens"], raw["labels"]

    docs = []
    for i, (sent, toks, labs) in enumerate(zip(sentences, tokens, labels)):
        sentence = sent[0] if isinstance(sent, (list, tuple)) else str(sent)
        toks = [str(t) for t in toks]
        labs = [int(l) for l in labs]
        assert len(toks) == len(labs), f"doc {i}: {len(toks)} tokens vs {len(labs)} labels"
        docs.append(
            Document(
                doc_id=i,
                sentence=sentence,
                words=toks,
                token_labels=labs,
                doc_label=1 if any(labs) else 0,
            )
        )
    return docs


def check_dataset(docs: list) -> dict:
    """Assertions from the paper (Sec. 4 / R10) and Definition 2 (R11)."""
    n = len(docs)
    n_anom = sum(d.doc_label for d in docs)
    n_norm = n - n_anom
    n_tok = sum(d.n_tokens for d in docs)
    n_pos = sum(sum(d.token_labels) for d in docs)
    # R11: doc anomalous iff at least one anomalous token
    for d in docs:
        assert d.doc_label == (1 if any(d.token_labels) else 0), f"doc {d.doc_id} label mismatch"
    # R10: 300 documents, 30 anomalous, 10% anomaly rate
    assert n == 300, f"expected 300 documents, got {n}"
    assert n_anom == 30, f"expected 30 anomalous documents, got {n_anom}"
    assert n_norm == 270, f"expected 270 normal documents, got {n_norm}"
    return {
        "n_docs": n,
        "n_normal_docs": n_norm,
        "n_anomalous_docs": n_anom,
        "doc_anomaly_rate": n_anom / n,
        "n_tokens": n_tok,
        "n_positive_tokens": n_pos,
        "token_positive_rate": n_pos / n_tok,
    }


def split_docs(docs: list, seed: int = 0, train_fraction: float = 0.5) -> Split:
    """50% of the *normal* documents form the memory-bank training set; the
    remaining normal documents plus every anomalous document form the test set
    (paper Sec. 6.1 / R6)."""
    normal = [d for d in docs if d.doc_label == 0]
    anomalous = [d for d in docs if d.doc_label == 1]
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    order = rng.permutation(len(normal))
    n_train = int(round(len(normal) * train_fraction))
    train_idx = set(order[:n_train].tolist())
    train = [normal[i] for i in range(len(normal)) if i in train_idx]
    test = [normal[i] for i in range(len(normal)) if i not in train_idx] + anomalous
    sp = Split(train=train, test=test, seed=seed, train_fraction=train_fraction)
    # R3: the training set must contain zero anomalous tokens
    assert sum(sum(d.token_labels) for d in sp.train) == 0, "anomalous token leaked into training"
    assert len(sp.train) + len(sp.test) == len(docs)
    return sp


def split_stats(sp: Split) -> dict:
    return {
        "seed": sp.seed,
        "train_fraction": sp.train_fraction,
        "n_train_docs": len(sp.train),
        "n_test_docs": len(sp.test),
        "n_test_normal_docs": sum(1 for d in sp.test if d.doc_label == 0),
        "n_test_anomalous_docs": sum(1 for d in sp.test if d.doc_label == 1),
        "n_train_tokens": sum(d.n_tokens for d in sp.train),
        "n_test_tokens": sum(d.n_tokens for d in sp.test),
        "n_test_positive_tokens": sum(sum(d.token_labels) for d in sp.test),
    }


def load_grammar_from_json(data_dir: Path | None = None) -> list:
    """Cross-check the .npy against the raw Label Studio export (informational)."""
    data_dir = Path(data_dir) if data_dir else DATA_DIR
    items = json.loads((data_dir / "grammar_correction_labeled.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    out = []
    for it in items:
        text = (it.get("data") or {}).get("text", "")
        anns = it.get("annotations") or []
        toks, labs = [], []
        if anns:
            res = sorted(anns[-1].get("result", []), key=lambda r: r.get("value", {}).get("start", 0))
            for r in res:
                v = r.get("value", {})
                toks.append(v.get("text", ""))
                lab = v.get("labels") or v.get("label") or []
                labs.append(int(lab[0]) if isinstance(lab, list) and lab else 0)
        out.append({"text": text, "tokens": toks, "labels": labs})
    return out

"""BERT-base-uncased front-end: word-level embeddings by element-wise max pooling
over the subwords of each word (paper Eq. 1 / R2, R9).

This is the batched equivalent of the authors' align.extract_word_embeddings
(the notebook ran it one sentence at a time on CUDA); the pooling rule is kept
identical: np.max over the stacked subword vectors of a word, special tokens
([CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD], word_id is None) are skipped.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

MODEL_NAME = "bert-base-uncased"
MAX_LENGTH = 128
BATCH_SIZE = 32


def _cache_dir() -> Path:
    root = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    base = Path(root) if root else Path(".cache")
    d = base / "tokencore_embeddings"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def _cache_key(model_name: str, docs) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha1()
    h.update(model_name.encode())
    for d in docs:
        h.update(repr((d.doc_id, d.sentence, tuple(d.words))).encode())
    return h.hexdigest()[:16]


def load_model(model_name: str = MODEL_NAME, device: str | None = None):
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    if device is None:
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    model = model.to(device).eval()
    return tok, model, device


@torch.no_grad()
def embed_documents(docs, tokenizer, model, device, batch_size: int = BATCH_SIZE,
                    max_length: int = MAX_LENGTH, verbose: bool = True):
    """Return (list[np.ndarray], list[list[int]]) : per-document word embedding
    matrices and the parallel gold token labels."""
    n_threads = int(os.environ.get("TOKEN_TORCH_THREADS", "0") or 0)
    if n_threads > 0:
        torch.set_num_threads(n_threads)

    word_embs, word_labels = [], []
    n_batches = (len(docs) + batch_size - 1) // batch_size
    for b in range(n_batches):
        chunk = docs[b * batch_size:(b + 1) * batch_size]
        enc = tokenizer(
            [d.words for d in chunk],
            is_split_into_words=True,
            padding=True,
            truncation=True,
            max_length=max_length,
            return_tensors="pt",
        )
        enc = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in enc.items()}
        out = model(input_ids=enc["input_ids"], attention_mask=enc["attention_mask"])
        hs = out.last_hidden_state  # (B, L, H)
        for i, d in enumerate(chunk):
            wids = enc.word_ids(batch_index=i)
            groups: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
            for pos, w in enumerate(wids):
                if w is None:
                    continue  # [CLS] / [SEP] / [PAD]
                groups.setdefault(w, []).append(pos)
            mat = np.zeros((len(d.words), hs.shape[-1]), dtype=np.float32)
            for w in sorted(groups):
                sub = hs[i, groups[w], :].cpu().numpy()
                mat[w] = np.max(sub, axis=0)  # element-wise max pooling, Eq. (1)
            missing = [w for w in range(len(d.words)) if w not in groups]
            if missing:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"doc {d.doc_id}: {len(missing)} gold words got no subword unit "
                    f"(truncation at max_length={max_length}?): {missing[:5]}"
                )
            word_embs.append(mat)
            word_labels.append(list(d.token_labels))
        if verbose:
            print(f"  embedded batch {b + 1}/{n_batches} ({len(chunk)} docs)", flush=True)
    return word_embs, word_labels


def get_embeddings(docs, model_name: str = MODEL_NAME, device: str | None = None,
                   use_cache: bool = True, verbose: bool = True):
    """Embed documents, caching the result under REPRO_DATA_CACHE (embeddings do
    not depend on the train/test split, so they are reused across seeds)."""
    key = _cache_key(model_name, docs)
    cache_file = _cache_dir() / f"{model_name.replace('/', '_')}_{key}.npz"
    if use_cache and cache_file.exists():
        blob = np.load(cache_file, allow_pickle=True)
        if verbose:
            print(f"  loaded cached embeddings from {cache_file}")
        return list(blob["embs"]), [list(l) for l in blob["labels"]]
    tok, model, device = load_model(model_name, device)
    embs, labels = embed_documents(docs, tok, model, device, verbose=verbose)
    if use_cache:
        np.savez_compressed(
            cache_file,
            embs=np.array(embs, dtype=object),
            labels=np.array(labels, dtype=object),
        )
        if verbose:
            print(f"  cached embeddings to {cache_file}")
    return embs, labels


def flatten(embs, labels):
    """Stack per-document matrices into one (n_tokens, dim) matrix + label list."""
    X = np.vstack([np.asarray(e, dtype=np.float64) for e in embs])
    y = [int(v) for lab in labels for v in lab]
    return X, y

"""Thin adapter over the authors' unmodified repo/TokenCore.py.

The authors' class is `TokenCore` (the notebook imports it as `TextCore` from a
`TextCore` module that is not shipped; the shipped file defines `TokenCore`).
Default configuration: n_neighbors=1, NearestNeighbors default metric
(minkowski p=2 == Euclidean), which is exactly Eq. (2) of the paper.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
AUTHOR_FILE = REPO / "repo" / "TokenCore.py"


def load_author_tokencore():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("authors_tokencore", AUTHOR_FILE)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    if not hasattr(mod, "TokenCore"):
        raise RuntimeError(f"{AUTHOR_FILE} does not define class TokenCore")
    return mod.TokenCore


class TokenCoreDetector:
    """Memory-bank detector: fit on normal-training token embeddings only (R3),
    score each test token by its distance to the nearest bank entry (R4)."""

    def __init__(self, n_neighbors: int = 1):
        self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
        self._cls = load_author_tokencore()
        self.model = None

    def fit(self, X_train: np.ndarray):
        assert len(X_train) > 0, "empty memory bank"
        self.model = self._cls(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors)
        self.model.fit(np.asarray(X_train, dtype=np.float64))
        self.n_bank = len(X_train)
        return self

    def decision_function(self, X_test: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        if self.model is None:
            raise RuntimeError("call fit() first")
        scores = np.asarray(self.model.decision_function(np.asarray(X_test, dtype=np.float64)))
        assert scores.shape == (len(X_test),), scores.shape
        assert np.all(np.isfinite(scores)), "non-finite token scores"
        return scores

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

import data_grammar  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert  # noqa: E402
import evaluate  # noqa: E402
from detector import TokenCoreDetector  # noqa: E402

SEEDS = list(range(10))


def split_all_docs(docs, seed):
    """Alternative reading: 50% of ALL documents, anomalous ones removed from train."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    order = rng.permutation(len(docs))
    n_train = len(docs) // 2
    train = [docs[i] for i in order[:n_train] if docs[i].doc_label == 0]
    test = [docs[i] for i in order[n_train:]]
    return train, test


def first_subword_embs(docs, model_name):
    """Re-embed taking only the first subword of each word (ablation)."""
    import torch
    from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name).eval()
    out = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for d in docs:
            enc = tok(d.words, is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors="pt",
                      truncation=True, max_length=embed_bert.MAX_LENGTH)
            hs = model(input_ids=enc["input_ids"], attention_mask=enc["attention_mask"]).last_hidden_state
            wids = enc.word_ids(batch_index=0)
            mat = np.zeros((len(d.words), hs.shape[-1]), dtype=np.float32)
            seen = set()
            for pos, w in enumerate(wids):
                if w is None or w in seen:
                    continue
                seen.add(w)
                mat[w] = hs[0, pos, :].numpy()
            out.append(mat)
    return out


def auroc(scores, labels):
    return evaluate.token_level_metrics(scores, labels)["auroc"]


def main():
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    data_grammar.check_dataset(docs)
    results = {}

    for model_name in ["bert-base-uncased", "bert-base-cased"]:
        embs, labels = embed_bert.get_embeddings(docs, model_name=model_name)
        by_id = {d.doc_id: (e, l) for d, e, l in zip(docs, embs, labels)}
        firsts = first_subword_embs(docs, model_name)
        first_by_id = {d.doc_id: f for d, f in zip(docs, firsts)}

        for seed in SEEDS:
            sp = data_grammar.split_docs(docs, seed=seed)
            tr, te = split_all_docs(docs, seed)
            key = f"{model_name}|seed{seed}"
            row = {}
            for tag, (train, test) in {
                "split_normal50": (sp.train, sp.test),
                "split_all50": (tr, te),
            }.items():
                Xtr = np.vstack([by_id[d.doc_id][0] for d in train])
                Xte = np.vstack([by_id[d.doc_id][0] for d in test])
                yte = [v for d in test for v in by_id[d.doc_id][1]]
                det = TokenCoreDetector(1).fit(Xtr)
                s = det.decision_function(Xte)
                row[f"{tag}|euclidean|maxpool"] = round(float(auroc(s, yte)), 4)
                from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
                nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1, metric="cosine").fit(Xtr)
                row[f"{tag}|cosine|maxpool"] = round(
                    float(auroc(nn.kneighbors(Xte)[0].flatten(), yte)), 4)
                Ftr = np.vstack([first_by_id[d.doc_id] for d in train])
                Fte = np.vstack([first_by_id[d.doc_id] for d in test])
                row[f"{tag}|euclidean|firstsub"] = round(
                    float(auroc(TokenCoreDetector(1).fit(Ftr).decision_function(Fte), yte)), 4)
            results[key] = row
            print(key, json.dumps(row), flush=True)

    # aggregate
    agg = {}
    for model_name in ["bert-base-uncased", "bert-base-cased"]:
        for variant in ["split_normal50|euclidean|maxpool", "split_all50|euclidean|maxpool",
                        "split_normal50|cosine|maxpool", "split_normal50|euclidean|firstsub"]:
            vals = [results[f"{model_name}|seed{s}"][variant] for s in SEEDS]
            agg[f"{model_name}|{variant}"] = {
                "mean": round(float(np.mean(vals)), 4),
                "std": round(float(np.std(vals)), 4),
                "min": round(float(np.min(vals)), 4),
                "max": round(float(np.max(vals)), 4),
            }
            print(f"{model_name}|{variant}: {agg[f'{model_name}|{variant}']}")

    out = {"per_seed": results, "aggregate": agg, "seeds": SEEDS}
    (ROOT / "state" / "variants.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print("wrote state/variants.json")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Alignment audit: for a few anomalous documents, print every scored word unit
next to its gold token label and its TokenCore score, and verify that the gold
anomalous span words are exactly the units being scored (no shift, no drop, no
duplication introduced by the subword grouping / max pooling / punctuation).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

import data_grammar  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert  # noqa: E402
from detector import TokenCoreDetector  # noqa: E402

N_DOCS = 3


def main():
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    data_grammar.check_dataset(docs)
    sp = data_grammar.split_docs(docs, seed=0)
    embs, labels = embed_bert.get_embeddings(docs, model_name=embed_bert.MODEL_NAME)
    by_id = {d.doc_id: (e, l) for d, e, l in zip(docs, embs, labels)}

    # 1:1 alignment between gold words and produced word units
    bad = 0
    for d in docs:
        e, l = by_id[d.doc_id]
        if e.shape[0] != len(d.words) or len(l) != len(d.words):
            bad += 1
            print("MISALIGNED doc", d.doc_id, e.shape, len(d.words), len(l))
    print(f"docs with word-unit count != gold word count: {bad} / {len(docs)}")

    # max-pooling really is the coordinate-wise max of the subword vectors
    import torch
    from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(embed_bert.MODEL_NAME)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(embed_bert.MODEL_NAME).eval()
    d = docs[270]  # an anomalous document
    with torch.no_grad():
        enc = tok(d.words, is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors="pt",
                  truncation=True, max_length=embed_bert.MAX_LENGTH)
        hs = model(input_ids=enc["input_ids"], attention_mask=enc["attention_mask"]).last_hidden_state
    wids = enc.word_ids(batch_index=0)
    groups = {}
    for pos, w in enumerate(wids):
        if w is None:
            continue
        groups.setdefault(w, []).append(pos)
    print("\nsubword grouping check on doc", d.doc_id, ":", d.sentence)
    for w in sorted(groups):
        sub = hs[0, groups[w], :].numpy()
        pooled = np.max(sub, axis=0)
        ref = by_id[d.doc_id][0][w]
        ok = np.allclose(pooled, ref, atol=1e-5)
        print(f"  word[{w}] {d.words[w]!r:14} subwords={[tok.convert_ids_to_tokens(enc['input_ids'][0][p].item()) for p in groups[w]]} "
              f"maxpool_matches={ok}")

    # score the test tokens and print the anomalous documents
    X_train = np.vstack([by_id[x.doc_id][0] for x in sp.train])
    det = TokenCoreDetector(1).fit(X_train)
    X_test = np.vstack([by_id[x.doc_id][0] for x in sp.test])
    y_test = [v for x in sp.test for v in by_id[x.doc_id][1]]
    scores = det.decision_function(X_test)

    print("\nper-document word-unit / label / score dump (anomalous test docs)")
    i = 0
    shown = 0
    for x in sp.test:
        n = x.n_tokens
        s, y = scores[i:i + n], y_test[i:i + n]
        i += n
        if not any(y):
            continue
        shown += 1
        if shown > N_DOCS:
            continue
        print(f"\n--- doc {x.doc_id}: {x.sentence}")
        print(f"    {'word':<16}{'gold':>5}{'score':>10}   rank_in_doc")
        order = np.argsort(-s)
        rank = {int(j): r for r, j in enumerate(order)}
        for j, w in enumerate(x.words):
            mark = "  <== GOLD ANOMALY" if y[j] == 1 else ""
            print(f"    {w:<16}{y[j]:>5}{s[j]:>10.3f}   {rank[j]}{mark}")
        print(f"    gold anomalous words: {[w for w, l in zip(x.words, y) if l == 1]}")
        print(f"    top-3 scored words:   {[x.words[int(j)] for j in order[:3]]}")
    print(f"\n(total anomalous test docs: {sum(1 for x in sp.test if x.doc_label == 1)})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""A9 sensitivity test: L2-normalise every word-level embedding before the
nearest-neighbour search (equivalent to a cosine metric for n_neighbors=1).

Everything else is frozen exactly as in the primary protocol:
  * same memory bank (every word-level embedding of every token of the 135
    normal training documents, no subsampling, no coreset)
  * same element-wise max pooling over subwords (Eq. 1)
  * same mean aggregation to document level (Eq. 3)
  * same 50%-of-normal split, seeds 0..9
Only the embedding scale changes.  No hyperparameter is tuned toward any
target number.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

import data_grammar  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert  # noqa: E402
import evaluate  # noqa: E402
from detector import TokenCoreDetector  # noqa: E402

SEEDS = list(range(10))


def l2(X):
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    n = np.linalg.norm(X, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    n[n == 0] = 1.0
    return X / n


def run(seed, X_all, by_id, docs, normalize):
    sp = data_grammar.split_docs(docs, seed=seed)
    Xtr = np.vstack([by_id[d.doc_id][0] for d in sp.train])
    Xte = np.vstack([by_id[d.doc_id][0] for d in sp.test])
    yte = [v for d in sp.test for v in by_id[d.doc_id][1]]
    if normalize:
        Xtr, Xte = l2(Xtr), l2(Xte)
    det = TokenCoreDetector(1).fit(Xtr)
    s = det.decision_function(Xte)
    tok = evaluate.token_level_metrics(s, yte)
    doc = evaluate.document_level_metrics(
        evaluate.document_scores(s, [d.n_tokens for d in sp.test]),
        [d.doc_label for d in sp.test])
    return tok, doc


def main():
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    data_grammar.check_dataset(docs)
    embs, labels = embed_bert.get_embeddings(docs, model_name=embed_bert.MODEL_NAME)
    by_id = {d.doc_id: (e, l) for d, e, l in zip(docs, embs, labels)}

    out = {"seeds": SEEDS, "per_seed": {}, "aggregate": {}}
    for seed in SEEDS:
        row = {}
        for tag, norm in [("raw_l2_metric", False), ("l2_normalized", True)]:
            tok, doc = run(seed, embs, by_id, docs, norm)
            row[tag] = {
                "token_auroc": round(float(tok["auroc"]), 4),
                "token_auprc": round(float(tok["auprc"]), 4),
                "doc_auroc": round(float(doc["auroc"]), 4),
                "doc_auprc": round(float(doc["auprc"]), 4),
            }
        out["per_seed"][f"seed{seed}"] = row
        print(f"seed {seed}: {json.dumps(row)}", flush=True)

    for tag in ["raw_l2_metric", "l2_normalized"]:
        for m in ["token_auroc", "token_auprc", "doc_auroc", "doc_auprc"]:
            vals = [out["per_seed"][f"seed{s}"][tag][m] for s in SEEDS]
            out["aggregate"].setdefault(tag, {})[m] = {
                "mean": round(float(np.mean(vals)), 4),
                "std": round(float(np.std(vals)), 4),
                "min": round(float(np.min(vals)), 4),
                "max": round(float(np.max(vals)), 4),
            }
        print(f"\n{tag}: {json.dumps(out['aggregate'][tag], indent=2)}")

    # equivalence check: L2-normalised + Euclidean NN == cosine NN
    sp = data_grammar.split_docs(docs, seed=0)
    Xtr = np.vstack([by_id[d.doc_id][0] for d in sp.train])
    Xte = np.vstack([by_id[d.doc_id][0] for d in sp.test])
    s_norm = TokenCoreDetector(1).fit(l2(Xtr)).decision_function(l2(Xte))
    from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
    s_cos = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1, metric="cosine").fit(Xtr).kneighbors(Xte)[0].flatten()
    print("\nL2+euclidean vs cosine-metric NN: max |score diff| =",
          float(np.max(np.abs(s_norm - s_cos))))

    (ROOT / "state" / "normalize_ablation.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2),
                                                            encoding="utf-8")
    print("wrote state/normalize_ablation.json")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Validate the (unreleased) split protocol against the authors' own frozen
notebook output.

Demo.ipynb cell 4 ends with `roc_auc` = 0.8291871975956033 for the
restaurant_review dataset (token-level AUROC, pooled over all test tokens,
bert-base-cased, authors' align.extract_word_embeddings + TextCore defaults).
The notebook's own log shows "Sentence 1/550" for BOTH the train and the test
pass, i.e. the split is 550/550 over the 1,100 released documents.

This script re-runs that exact computation with our rebuilt driver under
several readings of the split and reports which one reproduces the frozen
value.  The frozen notebook output is the authors' released code output, not a
number taken from the paper's tables.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

import data_grammar as dg  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert  # noqa: E402
import evaluate  # noqa: E402
from detector import TokenCoreDetector  # noqa: E402

FROZEN = 0.8291871975956033
SEEDS = list(range(10))


def load_review():
    d = np.load(dg.DATA_DIR / "restaurant_review.npy", allow_pickle=True).item()
    docs = []
    for i, (sent, toks, labs) in enumerate(zip(d["sentences"], d["tokens"], d["labels"])):
        docs.append(dg.Document(i, sent[0] if isinstance(sent, list) else sent,
                                list(toks), [int(v) for v in labs],
                                1 if any(labs) else 0))
    return docs


def variants(docs, seed):
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    order = list(rng.permutation(len(docs)))
    n = len(docs) // 2
    plain_tr = [docs[i] for i in order[:n]]
    plain_te = [docs[i] for i in order[n:]]

    # stratified 50/50 per class
    normal = [i for i, d in enumerate(docs) if d.doc_label == 0]
    anom = [i for i, d in enumerate(docs) if d.doc_label == 1]
    r2 = np.random.RandomState(seed + 1000)
    r2.shuffle(normal)
    r2.shuffle(anom)
    k_n, k_a = len(normal) // 2, len(anom) // 2
    strat_tr = [docs[i] for i in normal[:k_n]] + [docs[i] for i in anom[:k_a]]
    strat_te = [docs[i] for i in normal[k_n:]] + [docs[i] for i in anom[k_a:]]

    sp = dg.split_docs(docs, seed=seed)  # 50% of normal only
    return {
        "plain50_all_docs": (plain_tr, plain_te),
        "stratified50": (strat_tr, strat_te),
        "normal50_only": (sp.train, sp.test),
        "plain50_drop_anom_train": ([d for d in plain_tr if d.doc_label == 0], plain_te),
    }


def main():
    docs = load_review()
    print(f"review docs={len(docs)} anomalous={sum(d.doc_label for d in docs)}")
    embs, labels = embed_bert.get_embeddings(docs, model_name="bert-base-cased")
    by_id = {d.doc_id: (e, l) for d, e, l in zip(docs, embs, labels)}

    out = {"frozen_notebook_value": FROZEN, "per_seed": {}, "aggregate": {}}
    for seed in SEEDS:
        row = {}
        for tag, (tr, te) in variants(docs, seed).items():
            Xtr = np.vstack([by_id[d.doc_id][0] for d in tr]).astype(np.float32)
            Xte = np.vstack([by_id[d.doc_id][0] for d in te]).astype(np.float32)
            yte = [v for d in te for v in by_id[d.doc_id][1]]
            det = TokenCoreDetector(1).fit(Xtr)
            s = det.decision_function(Xte)
            row[tag] = {
                "token_auroc": round(float(evaluate.token_level_metrics(s, yte)["auroc"]), 4),
                "n_train_docs": len(tr), "n_test_docs": len(te),
                "n_train_anom_docs": sum(d.doc_label for d in tr),
            }
        out["per_seed"][f"seed{seed}"] = row
        print(f"seed {seed}: {json.dumps(row)}", flush=True)

    for tag in ["plain50_all_docs", "stratified50", "normal50_only", "plain50_drop_anom_train"]:
        vals = [out["per_seed"][f"seed{s}"][tag]["token_auroc"] for s in SEEDS]
        out["aggregate"][tag] = {
            "mean": round(float(np.mean(vals)), 4), "std": round(float(np.std(vals)), 4),
            "min": round(float(np.min(vals)), 4), "max": round(float(np.max(vals)), 4),
            "n_train_docs": out["per_seed"]["seed0"][tag]["n_train_docs"],
            "n_test_docs": out["per_seed"]["seed0"][tag]["n_test_docs"],
            "n_train_anom_docs": out["per_seed"]["seed0"][tag]["n_train_anom_docs"],
        }
        print(f"\n{tag}: {json.dumps(out['aggregate'][tag])}")

    (ROOT / "state" / "review_split_validation.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2),
                                                                 encoding="utf-8")
    print("\nwrote state/review_split_validation.json")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Re-assert the 1:1 word-unit-to-gold-word map on all three released datasets
with the authors' max_length (BertTokenizer default = 512)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

import data_grammar as dg  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert  # noqa: E402


def load(name):
    d = np.load(dg.DATA_DIR / f"{name}.npy", allow_pickle=True).item()
    docs = []
    for i, (sent, toks, labs) in enumerate(zip(d["sentences"], d["tokens"], d["labels"])):
        docs.append(dg.Document(i, sent[0] if isinstance(sent, list) else sent,
                                list(toks), [int(v) for v in labs], 1 if any(labs) else 0))
    return docs


for name in ["grammar", "restaurant_review", "sms_spam"]:
    docs = load(name)
    embs, labels = embed_bert.get_embeddings(docs, model_name=embed_bert.MODEL_NAME,
                                             verbose=False)
    ok = sum(1 for d, e, l in zip(docs, embs, labels)
             if e.shape[0] == len(d.words) == len(l))
    dims = {e.shape[1] for e in embs}
    print(f"{name}: docs={len(docs)} aligned={ok}/{len(docs)} "
          f"dims={dims} tokens={sum(e.shape[0] for e in embs)} "
          f"pos={sum(sum(l) for l in labels)}")

def decision_function(self, X, chunk_size: int = 2048) -> np.ndarray:
        """Distance from each row of X to its nearest memory-bank entry (Eq. 2).

        The query is issued in chunks so that the (n_query x n_bank) distance
        matrix is never materialised at once; per-row nearest neighbours are
        independent, so chunking does not change the result.
        """
        X = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
        out = np.empty(len(X), dtype=np.float64)
        for i in range(0, len(X), chunk_size):
            out[i:i + chunk_size] = self.nn.kneighbors(X[i:i + chunk_size])[0].flatten()
        return out

"""Validate the rebuilt driver against the authors' own frozen notebook output.

Demo.ipynb cell 4 ends with `roc_auc` = 0.8291871975956033 for the
restaurant_review dataset (token-level AUROC pooled over all test tokens,
bert-base-cased, authors' align.extract_word_embeddings + TextCore defaults).
The notebook's own log shows "Sentence 1/550" for both the train and the test
pass, i.e. a 550/550 split of the 1,100 released documents.

This script re-runs that computation with the rebuilt driver under the paper's
split protocol (R6: 50% of the NORMAL documents as the memory-bank training set)
and reports the 10-seed mean/std.  The frozen notebook output is the authors'
released code output, not a number taken from the paper's tables.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

import data_grammar as dg  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert  # noqa: E402
import evaluate  # noqa: E402
from detector import TokenCoreDetector  # noqa: E402

FROZEN = 0.8291871975956033
SEEDS = list(range(10))


def load_review():
    d = np.load(dg.DATA_DIR / "restaurant_review.npy", allow_pickle=True).item()
    docs = []
    for i, (sent, toks, labs) in enumerate(zip(d["sentences"], d["tokens"], d["labels"])):
        docs.append(dg.Document(i, sent[0] if isinstance(sent, list) else sent,
                                list(toks), [int(v) for v in labs],
                                1 if any(labs) else 0))
    return docs


def main():
    docs = load_review()
    embs, labels = embed_bert.get_embeddings(
        docs, model_name=embed_bert.MODEL_NAME, verbose=True,
        max_length=embed_bert.DATASET_MAX_LENGTH["restaurant_review"])
    by_id = {d.doc_id: (e, l) for d, e, l in zip(docs, embs, labels)}

    res = {}
    for seed in SEEDS:
        sp = dg.split_docs(docs, seed=seed)
        Xtr = np.vstack([by_id[d.doc_id][0] for d in sp.train])
        Xte = np.vstack([by_id[d.doc_id][0] for d in sp.test])
        yte = [v for d in sp.test for v in by_id[d.doc_id][1]]
        det = TokenCoreDetector(n_neighbors=1).fit(Xtr)
        s = det.decision_function(Xte)
        m = evaluate.token_level_metrics(s, yte)
        res[seed] = m
        print(f"seed {seed}: token AUROC={m['auroc']:.4f} AUPRC={m['auprc']:.4f} "
              f"bank={det.n_bank} test_tokens={m['n']} pos={m['n_positive']}", flush=True)

    a = np.array([res[s]["auroc"] for s in SEEDS])
    p = np.array([res[s]["auprc"] for s in SEEDS])
    out = {
        "frozen_notebook_roc_auc": FROZEN,
        "per_seed": {str(s): res[s] for s in SEEDS},
        "token_auroc_mean": float(a.mean()), "token_auroc_std": float(a.std()),
        "token_auprc_mean": float(p.mean()), "token_auprc_std": float(p.std()),
    }
    (ROOT / "state" / "review_validation.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(out, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in out.items() if k != "per_seed"}, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

target.statement: TokenCore token-level AUROC on the Grammar dataset
target.table_ref: Table 1, Token section, row TokenCore, column Grammar ROC

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The target experiment is implemented faithfully: Grammar data from the authors' released grammar.npy, 50%-of-normal training split, BERT-base-uncased last hidden states with element-wise max pooling, a full normal-token memory bank, Euclidean nearest-neighbor token scores, and mean document aggregation. The clean rerun computes token AUROC 0.5978 and AUPRC 0.0346 on 1544 test tokens with 47 positives, so the target AUROC is 0.0393 below the paper's 0.6371 and outside the 0.02 tolerance. The code contains paper reference constants, but they are confined to a labeled pass_fail/reference block and are not used as the computed result. The main fidelity gap is that only TokenCore is run; the six baseline methods required for the full table/ranking are absent. The discrepancy is best attributed to the unspecified split seed and other unspecified protocol details, not to a different dataset, metric, or method.

requirement_check.evidence: TokenCore uses bert-base-uncased last_hidden_state embeddings with max pooling, but no baseline implementations are present, so the 'all methods' part is not exercised.
src/embed_bert.py groups subwords via tokenizer.word_ids and applies np.max(sub, axis=0) per word (Eq. 1); alignment checks confirm one unit per gold word.
split_docs trains only on normal documents; reproduce.py asserts sum(y_train)==0; clean rerun bank=1202 normal-training tokens.
evaluate.document_scores averages token scores per document; metrics report document-level AUROC/AUPRC.
clean rerun split: 135 of 270 normal docs train, 165 test (135 normal + 30 anomalous); matches 50%-of-normal training rule.
metrics.json reports token_level and document_level AUROC and AUPRC; clean rerun prints both levels.
Only TokenCore is implemented/run; no LOF, iForest, ECOD, DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder, or LUNAR baselines appear in the code or metrics.
check_alignment.py/check_alignment_all.py verify word-unit count equals gold word count; clean rerun scores 1544 word-level test tokens aligned to 47 gold positives.
dataset_stats: 300 docs, 270 normal, 30 anomalous, anomaly rate 0.1; load_grammar/check_dataset enforce these counts.
Document.doc_label = 1 if any(token_labels) else 0; check_dataset asserts doc label equals any-token anomaly.
